lines: Bilateral hand tremors for 5 years, worse with action
She reports that the tremors are more noticeable when she is holding objects, like a cup of coffee or writing with a pen, and they seem to improve when her hands are at rest.
Her past medical history is significant for hypertension.
She takes for which she takes hydrochlorothiazide.
Her father had a similar tremor that began in his late 50s.
Smoking: Never smoker. Alcohol: Occasional. Occupation: Retired administrative assistant.
She denies any weakness, numbness, or other neurological symptoms.
On examination, you observe a fine, bilateral, postural tremor of her hands that worsens when she extends her arms and during finger-to-nose testing.
There is no rigidity, bradykinesia, or other abnormal movements.
Routine blood work including thyroid function tests and liver enzymes are within normal limits.

encounters.cc: Progressive shortness of breath and wheezing over 6 months

lines: Progressive shortness of breath and wheezing over 6 months
The patient is a 65-year-old female with HTN, CKD, RA, and asthma last evaluated in Neurology three months ago for tremor.
She reports a 6-month history of progressive shortness of breath, especially on exertion, and a wheezing sound that she notices mostly at night.
She reports that her symptoms are partially relieved by over-the-counter albuterol inhaler, which she started using a month ago on her neighbor's suggestion.
She has no history of atopic disease.
She takes hydrochlorothiazide, over-the-counter albuterol inhaler.
On physical examination, you note a respiratory rate of 22 breaths per minute, and auscultation of the lungs reveals bilateral expiratory wheezes.
Spirometry shows a forced expiratory volume in 1 second (FEV1) of 65% predicted, which improves to 80% predicted after administration of a bronchodilator.
The diffusion capacity for carbon monoxide (DLCO) is within normal limits.

encounters.cc: Multiple new red papules on trunk noticed over past year

lines: Multiple new red papules on trunk noticed over past year
This 65-year-old female with essential tremor and asthma presents to Dermatology following recent Neurology and Pulmonology care.
She reports that over the past year, she has noticed multiple small, bright red papules on her trunk.
She is concerned because they seem to be increasing in number.
She denies any pain, itching, or bleeding from the lesions.
Her medical history is significant for hypertension.
She takes for which she takes hydrochlorothiazide.
Smoking: Never smoker. Alcohol: Occasional. Occupation: Retired administrative assistant.
On physical examination, you note numerous 1-3 mm, round, non-blanching, bright red papules scattered over her chest and abdomen.
There are no similar lesions on her palms, soles, or mucous membranes.
The remainder of the examination is unremarkable.
Complete blood count: within normal limits
- Comprehensive metabolic panel: within normal limits

encounters.cc: Annual wellness visit with questions about cervical cancer screening

lines: Annual wellness visit with questions about cervical cancer screening
She returns for annual wellness visit with essential tremor and asthma.
She has no complaints, is up to date with all recommended vaccinations, and inquires about the need for continued Pap testing.
Her past medical history is significant for hypertension, controlled with lisinopril, and hyperlipidemia, managed with atorvastatin.
Her last Pap smear 3 years ago was normal, and she has had normal Pap smears consistently every 3 years since the age of 30.
She has no family history of gynecologic cancers.
She has never smoked and denies any history of sexually transmitted infections.
Her physical examination, including a pelvic exam, is unremarkable.

encounters.cc: Progressive fatigue and dyspnea with exertion over several months

lines: Progressive fatigue and dyspnea with exertion over several months
Hypertensive patient with asthma presents with progressive fatigue and dyspnea with exertion over the past several months.
She has a long-standing history of poorly controlled hypertension but no known history of coronary artery disease.
Her medications include amlodipine and hydrochlorothiazide, but she admits to missing doses regularly.
Smoking: Never smoker. Alcohol: Occasional. Occupation: Retired administrative assistant.
On physical examination, her blood pressure is 158/90 mm Hg, pulse is 82/min, and respirations are 16/min.
Cardiac auscultation reveals a sustained point of maximal impulse.

encounters.cc: Request to withdraw from clinical research study after 3 months

lines: Request to withdraw from clinical research study after 3 months
The patient is a 67-year-old female with rheumatoid arthritis, essential tremor, and hypertensive heart disease who returns to Rheumatology requesting withdrawal from a clinical research study.
She previously presented to Cardiology six months ago with progressive fatigue and dyspnea with exertion.
She has been participating in a Phase III clinical trial investigating a new biologic agent for inflammatory arthritis.
She enrolled 3 months ago after meeting eligibility criteria and signed a detailed informed consent document.
Since starting the study, she has noticed mild improvement in her joint stiffness, but she also feels increasingly fatigued and frustrated by the weekly clinic visits and frequent blood draws.
The physician overseeing the study is notified and comes in to speak with her.
- Hypertensive Heart Disease with End-Organ Damage (indication for echocardiography) (diagnosed 2022-01-15)
Smoking: Never smoker. Alcohol: Occasional. Occupation: Retired administrative assistant.
The patient does not appear distressed or confused and makes it clear that she no longer wishes to continue.
She does not ask any specific questions, nor does she offer further explanation.
The physician wants to handle the matter ethically and appropriately.

lines: Generalized weakness and recurrent muscle cramps for 1 week

- Hypertensive Heart Disease with End-Organ Damage (indication for echocardiography) (diagnosed 2022-01-15)
- Voluntary withdrawal from clinical research protocol (diagnosed 2022-07-15)
She reports adherence to her medication regimen, which includes hydrochlorothiazide for blood pressure control.
Smoking: Never smoker. Alcohol: Occasional. Occupation: Retired administrative assistant.
Her blood pressure is 145/90 mmHg, heart rate is 88 beats per minute
On examination, she appears mildly dehydrated.
Neurological examination reveals decreased muscle strength in her lower extremities and diminished deep tendon reflexes.
An electrocardiogram (ECG) shows U waves, flattened T waves, and occasional premature ventricular contractions.

encounters.cc: Sudden severe headache, nausea, and blurred vision in right eye after movie

lines: Sudden severe headache, nausea, and blurred vision in right eye after movie
Patient is a 68-year-old female with HTN, CKD, and asthma who returns to the ED with headache that began several hours ago after attending a movie premiere.
She describes the pain as throbbing and localized around her right eye, rating it as 9 out of 10 in intensity.
- Hypertensive Heart Disease with End-Organ Damage (indication for echocardiography) (diagnosed 2022-01-15)
- Voluntary withdrawal from clinical research protocol (diagnosed 2022-07-15)
- Hypokalemia managed with oral replacement (tolerating PO intake) (diagnosed 2023-01-15)
Her past medical history is significant for hypertension.
Smoking: Never smoker. Alcohol: Occasional. Occupation: Retired administrative assistant.
On physical examination, her right eye is red with conjunctival injection, and the cornea appears hazy.
The pupil of the affected eye is mid-dilated and non-reactive to light.
Palpation of the globe reveals a firm eyeball.
Visual acuity is decreased in the right eye compared to the left.
Intraocular pressure measured by tonometry is 48 mmHg in the right eye and 15 mmHg in the left eye.
Gonioscopy of the right eye shows a closed angle.
